This page details the '''records and statistics of the [[Copa Sudamericana]]''' football tournament. The Copa Sudamericana is an international club tournament played annually in South America. It includes three to eight teams from all ten [[CONMEBOL]] members. It is typically held from August to December and consists of six stages. The all-time leader in titles won are Argentina's [[Boca Juniors]], [[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] and [[Club Atlético Lanús|Lanús]], Ecuador's [[Independiente del Valle]] and [[LDU Quito]], and Brazil's [[Club Athletico Paranaense|Athletico Paranaense]], with two titles each.

===Unbeaten sides===
*Five clubs have won the Copa Sudamericana unbeaten:
**{{fbaicon|CHI}} [[Club Universidad de Chile|Universidad de Chile]] had 10 wins and 2 draws in [[2011 Copa Sudamericana|2011]]
**{{fbaicon|BRA}} [[São Paulo FC|São Paulo]] had 5 wins and 5 draws in [[2012 Copa Sudamericana|2012]]
**{{fbaicon|ARG}} [[Club Atlético River Plate|River Plate]] had 8 wins and 2 draws in [[2014 Copa Sudamericana|2014]]
**{{fbaicon|ARG}} [[Defensa y Justicia]] had 6 wins and 3 draws in [[2020 Copa Sudamericana|2020]]
**{{fbaicon|ECU}} [[C.S.D. Independiente del Valle|Independiente del Valle]] had 6 wins and 1 draw in [[2022 Copa Sudamericana|2022]]

===Finals success rate===
{{see also|List of Copa Sudamericana finals}}
Four clubs has appeared in the finals of the Copa Sudamericana more than once with a 100% success rate:
*[[Boca Juniors]] ([[2004 Copa Sudamericana|2004]], [[2005 Copa Sudamericana|2005]])
*[[Club Atlético Independiente|Independiente]] ([[2010 Copa Sudamericana|2010]], [[2017 Copa Sudamericana|2017]])
*[[Club Athletico Paranaense|Athletico Paranaense]] ([[2018 Copa Sudamericana|2018]], [[2021 Copa Sudamericana|2021]])
*[[Independiente del Valle]] ([[2019 Copa Sudamericana|2019]], [[2022 Copa Sudamericana|2022]])
Ten clubs have appeared in the final once, being victorious on that occasion:
*[[Club Atlético San Lorenzo de Almagro|San Lorenzo]] ([[2002 Copa Sudamericana|2002]])
*[[Cienciano]] ([[2003 Copa Sudamericana|2003]])
*[[C.F. Pachuca|Pachuca]] ([[2006 Copa Sudamericana|2006]])
*[[Arsenal de Sarandí|Arsenal]] ([[2007 Copa Sudamericana|2007]])
*[[Internacional de Porto Alegre|Internacional]] ([[2008 Copa Sudamericana|2008]])
*[[Club Universidad de Chile|Universidad de Chile]] ([[2011 Copa Sudamericana|2011]])
*[[Independiente Santa Fe|Santa Fe]] ([[2015 Copa Sudamericana|2015]])
*[[Associação Chapecoense de Futebol|Chapecoense]] ([[2016 Copa Sudamericana|2016]])
*[[Defensa y Justicia]]  ([[2020 Copa Sudamericana|2020]])
*[[Racing Club de Avellaneda|Racing]] ([[2024 Copa Sudamericana|2024]])
On the other end, fifteen clubs have appeared in the finals and have never won the tournament. One of those clubs has appeared in the finals more than once, losing on each occasion:
*[[Atlético Nacional]] ([[2002 Copa Sudamericana|2002]], [[2014 Copa Sudamericana|2014]], [[2016 Copa Sudamericana|2016]])

===Consecutive participations===
[[C.S. Emelec|Emelec]] have the record number of consecutive participations with 8 from 2009 to 2016.

=== Goals ===
==== Biggest wins ====
*[[Oriente Petrolero]] 1&ndash;10 [[Fluminense]] (May 26, 2022, also largest away win)
*[[Defensor Sporting]] 9&ndash;0 [[Sport Huancayo]] (September 16, 2010)<ref>http://www.conmebol.com/conmebol/mainMedia.html?id=16700&viewpage='full' {{Dead link|date=February 2022}}</ref>

==== Biggest two leg win ====
*[[L.D. Alajuelense|Alajuelense]] 2&ndash;11 [[Colo-Colo]] ([[2006 Copa Sudamericana]])

===Consecutive finals===
One team has appeared in a record of two consecutive finals:
*[[Boca Juniors]] ([[2004 Copa Sudamericana|2004]], [[2005 Copa Sudamericana|2005]])

===Successful defending===
Only one club have successfully defended the trophy: [[Boca Juniors]] ([[2005 Copa Sudamericana|2005]])
